source: Kreidberg et al. (2019), Nature 573, 87, 'Absence of a thick atmosphere on the terrestrial exoplanet LHS 3844b' (doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1497-4; arXiv:1908.06834). Spitzer IRAC channel 2 (4.5 um) phase curve, 100 hours between UT 2019 February 4 and 8, program 14204. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source, main text: eclipse depth, peak-to-trough amplitude of the phase variation, longitude of peak brightness and radius ratio of their adopted fit, a first-degree spherical-harmonic temperature map. The paper prints the fit as those three numbers, which are drawn here as one sinusoid; its Methods say a sinusoid differs from the spherical-harmonic model only through the Planck function. The paper does not state which way its longitude runs; east-positive is taken, and the value is one sigma from zero.

model.equation: f(phi) = F0 - A cos(phi - Delta phi), phi the orbital phase from transit; the text prints the peak-to-trough amplitude and the longitude of peak brightness.

semiAmplitude.cell: 350 +/- 40 ppm peak-to-trough: half of it is the semi-amplitude, 175 ppm
semiAmplitude.where: main text, peak-to-trough amplitude of the phase variation

offsetDegreesEast.where: main text, longitude of peak brightness

offsetDegrees.where: main text, longitude of peak brightness
